### T-257 — The realm's remaining collections: secrets, assets and the contribution arrays

> _2026-10-06 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

externalServices is a map now, and it was the one that mattered: it is the only collection the
suite's own config and a tenant's CR both declare, so it is the only one a merge can combine. The
rest of the rule is still outstanding and the cost differs per field, which is worth knowing before
starting. secrets and assets (IPlanOptions, IPlanConfig, IGeneratorEntry) are declared by a suite's
config and by its server.ts, so they merge too and belong in the same shape: keyed by the entry
name, which the entry already carries, so the change is IGeneratorEntry minus its name plus the two
plan-building sites and the fixtures. The contribution arrays in IComponentK8sConfig (k8sPorts,
k8sIngresses, k8sSecrets, k8sAssets, k8sVolumes) are declared by _no realm at all_ today - one file
mentions them, this one - so converting them is free now and expensive once realms carry them: do it
when the contract is next touched. Two fields are worth leaving as lists and saying so where they
are declared: k8sEnv is a list of name and value pairs whose order is the configuration's, and
k8sManifests is a list of raw manifests whose identity is kind plus name inside the object, so an
alias would be a second name for the same thing and a merge by alias could combine two different
kinds. The conversion itself is mechanical but touches four places at once - the type, the schema
the CRD declares, the generator, and the fixtures plus the pinned tree snapshot - and the fixtures
are the trap: the plan carries the _resolved_ list while the declaration is a map, so a test that
builds a plan directly needs a list, and converting those to a map is what the first attempt did
wrong (the suite answered 'plan.externalServices is not iterable').

### T-249 — The realm's other collections: externalServices is a map, the rest is T-257

> _2026-10-06 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

externalServices is converted and the CRD, the CR the tree writes and the ExternalName Service

its cost measured, is T-257: secrets and assets merge as well and want the same shape, the six
contribution arrays in IComponentK8sConfig are declared by no realm yet so converting them is free,
and k8sEnv (an ordered list of name and value pairs) and k8sManifests (raw manifests whose identity

### T-258 — The operator serves the read API; the page is the half left

> _2026-10-06 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

Decided by the user: the operator serves the deployment realm's read API, because it already runs
the realm and holds the namespaced read rights. Landed: the operator's container declares its RPC
port (declared because a Service has to name something to send to) and the install tree publishes
services/blong-operator.yaml - ClusterIP on 8091, selected by the operator's own instance and
part-of labels, so another namespace's operator is not selected by it. The address therefore belongs
to the cluster rather than to a tenant, which is the same reason the operator is installed once, and
it is the only shape that works: an Ingress backend has to be a Service in its own namespace and a
selector is namespace-local, so a suite's portal cannot front the operator and an ExternalName alias
is not routable as an ingress backend. The tree asserts the Service, its selector and its port. What
is left is the browser half rather than the API half: the page that reads that address needs a
bundle (the realm has index.html and a browser entry, so the vite build exists as a step) and a
static root served by the operator, and a tenant reaching it needs either an install-level host or
the page served by the operator's own gateway.

### T-273 — A relative gateway.static.root crashes the port

> _2026-10-08 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

Found while adding the static-root accessor (T-246). `@fastify/static` requires an absolute `root`
and throws FastifyError "root option must be an absolute path" at start, so a suite that names
`dist` or `./dist` in its release block takes the whole process down rather than serving nothing,
while the plugin own default (`path.join(process.cwd(), "dist")`) is absolute and works. Either the
plugin should resolve a configured root against the process working directory, the way its default
already does, or the config schema should refuse a relative one with a message that says so; the
first is one `path.resolve` in `core/blong-gogo/src/static.ts` and the second is a schema change.
Nothing names a relative root today — the suite absolute path is what the e2e covers — which is why
it was found by a test fixture rather than by a deployment.

### T-278 — The operator rollout wait runs before the restart that would fix it

> _2026-10-08 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

k3d-e2e.sh waits for the operator's rollout right after applying the install tree, to keep the stale
pod from writing the key pair it knows over the one just renewed, and REFRESH — which is what
replaces that pod — comes later. A pod already in a crash loop therefore blocks the run for the full
300s timeout and fails it before REFRESH is reached, even though the tree, the image and the
artifacts are all current, which is the trap F-439 records. The wait is worth keeping and worth
reordering or softening: the meaningful assertion is the one after REFRESH, since that is the pod
the tenant tree is generated by, so a failure before it can report what the restart was about to
fix. Either restart the operator as part of the apply (the refreshed image is already imported by
then) or tolerate the timeout here and let the post-REFRESH wait be the one that fails.

### T-283 — A changed Job cannot be re-applied over a failed one

> _2026-10-09 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

A Job pod template is immutable, so `kubectl apply` refuses a tree whose migration container changed
while the previous attempt is still there, and the run fails at the apply instead of retrying the
step. The operator has an update path that knows how to replace an attempt; the runbook applies
plainly. The smallest fix is `kubectl delete job --ignore-not-found` before the apply, and it should
be decided together with whether a failed attempt keeps its pod for a reader.

### T-284 — The artifact volume is replaced in place; an atomic swap would remove the race

> _2026-10-09 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

The prefetch unpacks into the version directory itself, so a reader that is already attached can see
a tree being rewritten, and the marker only narrows that window. Unpacking into a sibling directory
and swapping it in with two renames would hand readers either the old complete tree or the new one,
and a consumer whose hostPath type is Directory would hold its pod until the swap lands. It needs a
decision about the leftover directory on each node (retention, disk), and it changes the volume
layout the operator and the CRD describe.

### T-300 — A pass whose generation fails leaves the previous status standing

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

The operator's passes were failing on nodes is forbidden while the CR kept reading Ready from the
pass that last succeeded, because the status is written only once the tree materializes. Report a

### T-302 — A bound PersistentVolumeClaim cannot be applied a second time

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

A pass that owns a claim the cluster already bound fails with spec is immutable after creation,
because the generated spec differs from the bound one — volumeName and storageClassName, which only
the cluster can fill. Decide how a pass should treat an existing claim: skip it when the spec
differs only in fields the cluster writes, or report it as a divergence rather than as a failed
step, so one claim cannot hold a whole pass in Failed.

### T-301 — A switched-off run's check sees the last deployment's leftovers

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

The observation stands; my first explanation of it did not. A run that switches a service off
honours the switch everywhere it generates — the regenerated base loses `services/mysql`, the tree
carries no workload, alias or namespace, and the CR it applies names the switch — so the residual
objects the run's check complains about are leftovers from the deployments that came before, not
something this tree asked for. Why the check sees them: it runs at the end of the runbook, and the
phase it waits for can be the previous pass's (T-300), so no pass has reconciled the tree this run
just wrote. A pass prunes what its declaration stopped naming — the operator runs with the
environment the tree gives it, and the CI job asserts exactly this: the alias and the credentials
copy go, while the workload in the services namespace stays (D-461) — so the residue clears on the
next pass rather than needing a hand. The dev script's drop deletes it at once instead of waiting,
and deletes the service with it.

### T-267 — The gateway key pair's Secret has no owner and outlives the suite

> _2026-10-07 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

Confirmed cause: `kustomizeGatewayKeysEnsure` creates the Secret with `metadata: {name, namespace}`
and no labels at all, so no listing can ever return it - the sweep selects
`app.kubernetes.io/part-of=<suite>`, and the pass of the kustomize e2e (run 38082949690, artifact
`kustomize-diagnostics`) reports `0 obsolete, 0 deleted` on every pass. The object is invisible
rather than spared, which is why it outlives the suite. The fix has to make it visible and spared at
once: stamp the suite's labels so a listing can see it, and give it a label that
`prunableByObsolescence` honours - the pass creates the Secret in the same pass that would otherwise
call it obsolete, and the only labels that filter honours today are the two counted retentions
(`VOLUME_RETENTION_LABEL`, `ATTEMPT_RETENTION_LABEL`), neither of which means "never remove this".

### T-317 — The switched-off service's credentials copy survives the prune

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-kustomize · open_

With mysql switched off, blong-suite keeps a mysql-credentials Secret the pass should have pruned,
and the e2e asserts it must go (D-461, D-462; `test/blong-int-kustomize/lib/checks.ts`,
`backingServicesCheck`, which reports `the credentials copy survived the switch in blong-suite`).
Ruled out by the run and by reading the code: the prune was requested and on, `Secret` is in
`RESOURCE_TYPE_BY_KIND` so `sweptResourceTypes()` covers it, `listingScopes` does create a
`secret@<tenant>` scope for a kind the tree no longer names, the listing selects
`app.kubernetes.io/part-of=<suite>` for every scope, `secret` is in the adapter's `API_OF_RESOURCE`
so `cluster.secret.find` is answered rather than silently skipped, `prunable` keeps objects whose
namespace is the tenant's, `prunableByObsolescence` only drops those carrying a retention label, and
the committed base
(`suite/blong-suite/system/kustomize/base/services/mysql/credentials-in-suite.yaml`) carries
`part-of: blong-suite` and a `spec-hash`. The artifact of run 38082949690 (`kustomize-diagnostics`)
then ruled out the selector as well: the operator's log tail carries
`reconcile: pass from cr, apply yes: 0 to create, 11 to update, 10 unchanged, 0 obsolete, 0 deleted`
and no tally, and the reconcile stamps its plan from the same `suiteName` it selects with
(`kustomizeReconcileRun.ts` lines 576-584 against `suiteLabels` in `generator.ts`), so the generator
and the selector agree on the value. Every pass reporting `0 obsolete` and `0 deleted` therefore
says that no swept listing returns anything at all, rather than that one object is missed - which
makes the listing call itself the remaining suspect, not the labels. The confirmed neighbour is
T-267: `kustomizeGatewayKeysEnsure` creates its Secret with no labels, so no listing can see it
either. The next step is a test that drives the pass against a mock cluster holding a
`part-of: blong-suite` Secret of a departed kind and asserts a delete is issued -
`testReconcileScope` covers `listingScopes` only, which is why the wiring can be wrong while the
realm's suite stays green.

## Done

### T-279 — The operator reports obsolete objects and never deletes them

> _2026-10-08 · realm/blong-kustomize · done_

A pass computes what the plan no longer mentions and reports the count in
status.lastResult.obsolete, and apply: true means it may change the cluster — but nothing deletes:
switching a service off leaves its Deployment, its Service, its claim and its namespace running, and
the operator counts them as obsolete beside a Ready. Measured on the dev cluster: after the switch
reached the CR, the objects stayed until they were deleted by hand, and two further passes created
nothing, so the plan was right and the cluster was stale. The namespace cannot go either, which is
why obsolete stayed at 1 once the rest was gone. This is a destructive action and a policy decision,
not a missing line: a reconcile that deletes what a declaration stopped naming is what makes a
switch mean something, and it is also what deletes a volume somebody was still reading. Decide the
policy (delete on reconcile, delete behind an explicit flag, or report only and document that a
switch-off is finished by hand) and say it in the CRD's field descriptions, because that is where a
tenant reads what a switch does.

Implemented as decided (D-461): a pass prunes the suite's namespace and nothing wider, prune travels
from the operator's Deployment (BLONG_CONTROLLER_PRUNE=true) through the loop to the pass, the
status reports the count it removed, and the alias a realm's config dials is deleted with the switch
while the workload in a namespace of its own is left and reported obsolete. Kept rather than removed
because three files cite this id, and the next entry would have taken it (F-442).

### T-277 — The plan resolves no databases, so the init script creates none

> _2026-10-08 · realm/blong-kustomize · done_

The generated init ConfigMap is written and mounted, but its content is a comment: the plan reads a
connection's database from the port's config, and blong-suite names its database (blong-integration)
inside the release block of server.ts, which a k3s planning run does not merge — the tree is planned
with the k8s intent while the database name lives in the rc the deployment is released with. A
deployment that points its connection at a generated MySQL therefore finds no database of the name
it dials, and the first thing that notices is the migration Job. Two routes, and the choice is worth
making deliberately: name the databases in the CR (the operator has them and could pass them into
the plan, which is the shape the descriptor's values.initScript already expects), or have the init
script read them at runtime from the rc the pod mounts. The second keeps one answer to what a
deployment connects to, which is the direction the rest of the config model goes in.

Resolved by the override the deployment owns: a service's config takes databases, merged with the
names the plan's connections resolved (deduplicated, connections first). blong-suite names
blong-integration in its kustomize config, the generated init ConfigMap carries the CREATE DATABASE
line, and the request travels in the CR so a reconcile keeps it. Kept rather than removed because
plan.md and the generator's comment cite this id (F-442).

### T-280 — Generated workloads choose no node, and node-local storage needs one chosen

> _2026-10-09 · realm/blong-kustomize · done_

The bases carry no nodeSelector, affinity or topology spread, so a generated workload is scheduled
wherever the cluster likes. That is right for a cluster whose storage is network-attached and wrong
for one whose storage is node-local: the claim binds on one node and the pod may land on another,
where the volume is simply not there. The dev cluster does not show it because it has one agent and
every generated claim so far bound there. Two ways to close it, and the choice is a deployment's
rather than a realm's: let a service's config name placement (a nodeSelector and tolerations through
values, which the base renders like any other placeholder), or document that a generated service is
for clusters whose class is portable and leave node pinning to an installation that needs it.
Recording it rather than picking, because the second answer is legitimate and the first is a schema
change to a descriptor that no deployment has asked for yet.

placement now reaches the pod spec, unit-verified and documented; the cluster path is the same one
the labels take

### T-281 — Decide how a deployment obtains a generated service's credentials

> _2026-10-09 · realm/blong-kustomize · done_

The last piece between a generated service and a deployment that dials it. The alias answers (the
runbook dials mysql by name and connects) and the service is told which database to create, so what
is left is the credentials: a generated Secret lives in the services namespace, and a consumer pod
cannot read a Secret from another namespace, so the values have to travel — a copy the realm writes
into the suite's namespace, or a Secret the deployment already owns and the generated service reads
instead (which the descriptor's credentials.secret override already supports, and which is what an
installation with its own database would do). The first is a mirroring rule the realm would have to
state (which services, when, and what happens to a rotated value); the second needs nothing new and
asks the deployment to keep one Secret in two places. Also open: the realm's config has to name the
alias and the database, which is a suite's own edit rather than a realm change — worth writing down
as the recipe a deployment follows, whichever route is chosen.

the generated credentials Secret is written beside the suite as well, asserted by the runbook and by
CI (D-462)

### T-282 — A pass never sweeps the kinds its tree stopped naming

> _2026-10-09 · realm/blong-kustomize · done_

The prune builds its groups from the resource types the tree names, so a kind that leaves the tree
is never looked up and its objects stay behind. The credentials copy a switched-off service wrote
into the suite's namespace is the case that found it: a Secret, in a tree with no Secret left in it.
Sweep the kinds a suite can own instead, excluding the install-owned ones, and keep version-named
objects out of obsolescence pruning so the volume-retirement step stays the one that decides them.

the sweep covers the kinds a suite can own and version-named objects are left to the retention step
(D-464); verified on the dev cluster, where the credentials copy is now pruned with the switch
